naming.private_prefix: leading underscore for private methods and module-level helpers
naming.notes: verb_noun pattern for functions (cmd_analyze, ask_for_code, analyze_codebase); leading underscore for private methods (_post, _discover_tools, _parse_sse_result, _extract_json)

type_annotations.return_annotations: always on public and private functions
type_annotations.builtin_generics: list[Path], dict — not List[Path] or Dict
type_annotations.notes: All function signatures are annotated. Internal variables are not annotated.

structure.import_grouping: stdlib first, then third-party, then local — each group separated by blank line
structure.class_method_order: init_first, then private helpers (underscore prefix), then public interface
structure.module_docstring: present on entry-point modules only, contains usage examples
structure.preferred_length: short — functions kept to one screen, early returns over nesting

error_handling.exit_style: sys.exit for CLI entry points; raise for library/internal code
error_handling.guard_style: early return — validity checks at the top, happy path at the bottom
error_handling.error_messages: f-string always, multi-line strings joined with implicit concat

strings_and_flow.comprehensions: used for filtering collections (any(...) in guards)
strings_and_flow.method_chaining: light — one or two chained calls at most (.get().splitlines())

comments.docstring_style: plain single-line for simple functions; multi-line with Flow: section for complex classes
comments.docstring_coverage: public functions and non-trivial private helpers
comments.inline_style: explain why, not what (e.g. '# Ricky's own instructions: give it explicit, complete prompts')
